name: Zephyranthes

project_scope.note: Two-species Master Plant Pool comparison. This lesson reuses the settled Amaryllidaceae family taxonomy reconciliation and does not change species range or admission status.

shared_genus_characters.where_to_look_first: Start at the flower side view: confirm the rain-lily architecture with a large 6-tepaled flower on a scape and an inferior ovary below the perianth. Then use stigma shape/position and perianth-tube proportions to separate the two project species.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Bulbous scapose herbs with basal linear leaves, a spathe-associated flower, 6 tepals, 6 stamens, and an inferior ovary in the project lesson.
shared_genus_characters.caution: Do not separate these two primarily by white/pink color. Both may show pink tones; reproductive geometry is more reliable.

comparison_matrix.chlorosolen: Capitate; among or very near the anthers, at most slightly exserted.
comparison_matrix.drummondii: 3-fid and included within the perianth tube.

comparison_matrix.chlorosolen: Tube about 3/4 or more of perianth length.
Absent or extremely short; much shorter than spathe.
comparison_matrix.drummondii: Usually evident, about 0.2–2 cm (occasionally longer), still shorter than spathe.

comparison_matrix.chlorosolen: Dull green, to about 5 mm wide.

species_cards.fast_rule: Capitate stigma near the anthers + very long narrow tube making up most of the flower.
species_cards.taxonomy_note: Older Cooperia drummondii is reconciled in the family module to Z. chlorosolen; do not create a duplicate learner concept.

species_cards.fast_rule: 3-fid stigma hidden inside the tube + broader funnel with a tube only about half the perianth length.
species_cards.taxonomy_note: Accepted project concept; keep distinct from the Cooperia drummondii synonym attached to Z. chlorosolen.

overlap_and_cautions: Both can have white flowers with pink flushing or tinges, so color is not a safe primary separator.
Measure proportions from a side view when possible; a face-on flower hides the tube, ovary, stigma position and pedicel.
Rare biflowered Z. drummondii specimens are documented by FNA, so flower count alone is not an absolute character.
The historical name Cooperia drummondii is a taxonomy trap: the project family module maps it to Z. chlorosolen, not to Z. drummondii.

look_alikes.name: Allium / Nothoscordum
look_alikes.separation: Project family lesson routes these through superior ovaries and usually a many-flowered umbel; Zephyranthes has an inferior ovary and large rain-lily flower architecture.

look_alikes.name: other rain lilies / former Habranthus concepts
look_alikes.separation: Use stigma form/position, perianth tube proportions, spathe and pedicel rather than flower color; escalate unfamiliar concepts to diagnostic review instead of forcing an ID.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.need: Show entire perianth tube, spathe and ovary in both species at comparable scale.
Sharp view of stigma and anthers.
Show pedicel, spathe and inferior ovary.
Blade width and surface/color at similar scale; use only as supporting evidence.
Label Cooperia drummondii → Zephyranthes chlorosolen and explicitly contrast with Z. drummondii.

media_guidance.note: Prefer existing project/user/Joey exact-species media if available for side-view and reproductive macros. Photo-polish worker owns acquisition; this module specifies roles only.
